strengths: Strong empirical results: outperforms OpenAI-o1 by 4.1% on ID benchmarks and 10.4% on OOD benchmarks while training more efficiently
Comprehensive evaluation across 8 ID tasks and 3 OOD benchmarks with multiple frontier baselines
Practical training efficiency improvements: achieves comparable performance with ~100 fewer training steps than GRPO/DAPO
Demonstrates small models (4B-8B) can be competitive with much larger systems on rule-based reasoning
Well-executed experimental work with detailed implementation details, reproducibility commitments (code/models), and five runs with standard deviations
Thoughtful data curation with principled selection of diverse tasks spanning different reasoning forms, depths, and rule formats
Clear presentation with effective visualizations of domain weight dynamics and learning trajectories
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: DADS is relatively incremental—dynamic sampling based on domain rewards via exponential moving average, similar to existing curriculum learning approaches
Test set leakage undermines confidence: paper acknowledges potential leakage of Qwen3 on BigBench Hard, undermining OOD generalization claims and reproducibility
Incomplete baseline comparison: DAPO is compared without its dynamic sampling component for fairness, but this removes a key element, making it unclear how much improvement comes from DADS
Narrow scope limits generalization: only evaluated on rule-based reasoning; no evidence approach works for other domains (math, code, commonsense); only Qwen3 base models tested
Scalability to larger models unaddressed: only tested on 4B-8B models; paper acknowledges larger model scalability remains unverified, limiting practical applicability

Insufficient analysis of method efficacy: limited ablation on DADS hyperparameters (τ, ϵ, α); unclear why different τ values for 4B vs 8B; lacks comparison with other curriculum strategies; missing deeper analysis of why DADS works
Long reasoning chains not addressed: paper acknowledges unclear performance on extensive rule compositions and deep logical deductions
Limited failure analysis: Table 8 shows negative examples but lacks systematic analysis of when/why method fails or identification of failure patterns
Potential hyperparameter sensitivity: domain weight initialization not discussed; sample distribution m within domains not clearly explained; minimal exploration of hyperparameter choices

strengths: Comprehensive evaluation across ID and OOD benchmarks with strong empirical results (4.1% ID, 10.4% OOD improvement over o1)
Valuable multi-domain dataset (RULECOLLECTION-32K) covering diverse reasoning types, formats, and complexity levels
Thorough experimental analysis including ablations, sample efficiency studies, difficulty stratification, and hyperparameter sensitivity
Practical efficiency gains (1.4× speedup vs DAPO) with computational details enabling reproducibility
Well-motivated training regularizations (entropy bonus disabling, KL removal, rule shuffling) to prevent memorization
Clear presentation with detailed hyperparameters, data sources, and implementation details for reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty of core method: DADS is straightforward exponential moving average + softmax reweighting without significant algorithmic innovation
Dataset constructed from existing public sources rather than new collection; 32K examples is modest for modern RL, with significant class imbalance (ProofWriter 7,997 vs Clutrr 268)
Fairness concerns in comparisons: frontier models (o1, o3-mini, Claude-3.7) evaluated zero-shot without fine-tuning on RULECOLLECTION-32K; no ablation isolating DADS vs. dataset contribution
Scalability unverified: only 4B and 8B models tested; frontier reasoning models are 70B+, limiting practical applicability

Concerning evaluation patterns: suspected test set leakage on BBH (acknowledged by authors), dramatic RULEREASONER-4B drops on harder difficulty levels, suspicious Coin Flip improvement (44.7%→95.1%), no statistical significance testing
Incomplete generalization analysis: Section 5.5 claims about 'meta introspection' are primarily qualitative with limited causal evidence for why DADS enables OOD generalization
DADS shows non-trivial hyperparameter sensitivity (Table 7); Algorithm 1 lacks depth and principled justification for exponential moving average + softmax design
Missing key ablations: no isolation of DADS contribution from dataset contribution, no justification for target reward = 1, limited exploration of simpler alternative scheduling strategies
